verses.zh: 这虔诚的事以后，亚述王西拿基立来侵入犹大，围困一切坚固城，想要攻破占据。
verses.en: After these faithful deeds were accomplished, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded Judah. He besieged the fortified cities, intending to seize them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he said to break into them for himself.”
verses.commentary:
32:1 This period of conflict is also recorded in

- 2 Kgs. 18:13-19,37

- Isa. 36:1-37:38

For Sennacherib, King of Assyria, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA.

It is somewhat surprising that after Hezekiah's "faithfulness" (BDB 41, i.e., his spiritual reforms) that Assyria
attacked. Usually invasion was a result of covenant disobedience. Here, it was

- a way to reveal YHWH's power and uniqueness to all the ANE

- a way to test Hezekiah (cf. 2 Chr. 32:31)

verses.zh: 希西家见西拿基立来，定意要攻打耶路撒冷，
verses.en: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had invaded and intended to attack Jerusalem,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and his face was for war against Jerusalem.”map For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
32:2-6 Hezekiah made several preparations for war. He trusted YHWH but he also prepared by

- cutting off the local spring so the Assyrian army would nave no water, v. 4

- rebuilding the part of the city wall that had been broken down by Joash, the King of Israel (cf. 2 Chr. 25:23; Isa. 22:9-11), v. 5

- building the towers on the wall higher, v. 5

- building two walls of fortification (location unknown)

- strengthening the Millo (i.e., supporting terraces of the old city; see note at 2 Chr. 11:8), v. 5

- making large numbers of weapons, v. 5

- appointing military officers over the militia, v. 6

verses.zh: 就与首领和勇士商议，塞住城外的泉源；他们就都帮助他。
verses.en: he consulted with his advisers and military officers about stopping up the springs[NOTE:1] outside the city, and they supported him.
notes: Heb “the waters of the springs.”

verses.zh: 于是有许多人聚集，塞了一切泉源，并通流国中的小河，说：「亚述王来，为何让他得着许多水呢？」
verses.en: A large number of people gathered together and stopped up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the district.[NOTE:1] They reasoned,[NOTE:2] “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?”
notes: Heb “and they closed up all the springs and the stream that flows in the midst of the land.” Here אָרֶץ (ʾarets, “land”) does not refer to the entire land, but to a smaller region like a district.
Heb “land, saying.”
verses.commentary:
32:4

NASB
"through the region"

NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, REB
"through the land"

NJB
"through the country"

LXX
"that separated the city"

Peshitta
"through the midst of the land"

The term "land" (BDB 75) has a wide semantic range.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

verses.zh: 希西家力图自强，就修筑所有拆毁的城墙，高与城楼相齐；在城外又筑一城，坚固大卫城的米罗，制造了许多军器、盾牌；
verses.en: Hezekiah[NOTE:1] energetically rebuilt[NOTE:2] every broken wall. He erected towers and an outer wall[NOTE:3] and fortified the terrace of the City of David.[NOTE:4] He made many weapons and shields.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Hezekiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “strengthened himself and built.”
Heb “and outside the wall another one.”
The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
verses.commentary:
32:5 "the city of David" This refers to the old city of the Jebusites or the citadel in its midst.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM

verses.zh: 设立军长管理百姓，将他们招聚在城门的宽阔处，用话勉励他们，说：
verses.en: He appointed military officers over the army[NOTE:1] and assembled them in the square at the city gate. He encouraged them,[NOTE:2] saying,
notes: Heb “and he placed officers of war over the people.”
Heb “he spoke to their heart[s].”

verses.zh: 「你们当刚强壮胆，不要因亚述王和跟随他的大军恐惧、惊慌；因为与我们同在的，比与他们同在的更大。
verses.en: “Be strong and brave! Don’t be afraid and don’t panic[NOTE:1] because of the king of Assyria and this huge army that is with him. We have with us one who is stronger than those who are with him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps, “and don’t be discouraged.”
Heb “for with us [is] a greater [one] than with him.”
verses.commentary:
32:7-8 The Chronicler records several speeches of godly Judean kings as a way to communicate theological truths.

This speech has several wonderful theological affirmations.

- encouragement of YHWH's help, so fear not

- be strong ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE

- be courageous ‒ BDB 54, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE

- do not fear ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- do not be dismayed ‒ BDB 369, KB 365, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- these same kinds of encouraging words were given:

(1) Moses to Joshua ‒ Deut. 31:7-8,23

(2) YHWH to Joshua ‒ Josh. 1:6,7,9; 10:8

(3) Joshua to his military ‒ Josh. 10:25

(4) David to Solomon ‒ 1 Chr. 22:13; 28:20

- theological truths

- the One with us is greater than the one with him (i.e., YHWH vs. Assyrian gods); notice similar imagery in 2 Kgs. 6:16;
Ps. 118:6; Rom. 8:31

- with him is only an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight
our battles (i.e., YHWH the Divine Warrior); notice similar imagery in Isa. 31:3; Jer. 17:5; there is more to reality than the
physical!

- the people relied on the words of Hezekiah

- they trusted their leader's words (cf. 2 Kgs. 18:5 for Hezekiah's faith)

- They trusted their God

- Isaiah 22 seems to criticize Hezekiah for his military preparations but Chronicles does not

verses.zh: 与他们同在的是肉臂，与我们同在的是耶和华―我们的　神，他必帮助我们，为我们争战。」百姓就靠犹大王希西家的话，安然无惧了。
verses.en: He has with him mere human strength,[NOTE:1] but the Lord our God is with us to help us and fight our battles!” The army[NOTE:2] was encouraged by the words of King Hezekiah of Judah.
notes: Heb “With him is an arm of flesh.”
Or “people.”

verses.zh: 此后，亚述王西拿基立和他的全军攻打拉吉，就差遣臣仆到耶路撒冷见犹大王希西家和一切在耶路撒冷的犹大人，说：
verses.en: Afterward King Sennacherib of Assyria, while attacking Lachish with all his military might, sent his messengers[NOTE:1] to Jerusalem. The message was for King Hezekiah of Judah and all the people of[NOTE:2] Judah who were in Jerusalem. It read:
notes: Heb “servants.”
Heb “all Judah.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the name “Judah” here by metonymy for the people of Judah.
verses.commentary:
32:9-15 The king of Assyria tried to instill fear in the defenders of Jerusalem with a loud public messge (cf. 2 Kings 18).

- What are you trusting? (v. 10)

- Asserting that Hezekiah had given them false hope. (v. 11)

- Reminding them that Hezekiah had taken away their local worship sites (i.e., high places). v. 12

- Look at our military victories, has any nation or their god been successful against us? (vv. 13-15, see note,
IVP Bible Background Commentary [OT], p. 455)

- Do not let Hezekiah

- deceive you ‒ BDB 674, KB 728, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVEe sense

- mislead you ‒ BDB 694, KB 749, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- do not believe him ‒ BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

32:9 Josephus, Antiq. 10.1.1., mentions the name of

- Sennacherib's military general as Rabshakeh

- his two commanders as

- Tartan

- Rab-saris (cf. 2 Kgs. 18:17)

Josephus says Sennacherib ignored his promise not to besiege Jerusalem in light of Hezekiah's offer to pay a
large tribute, mostly from the temple (cf. 2 Kgs. 18:13-16), but instead he attacked Egypt and Ethiopia but left a large military
contingent to attack and destroy Jerusalem. Chronicles never mentions this attempted bribe of Hezekiah's.

verses.zh: 「亚述王西拿基立如此说：『你们倚靠甚么，还在耶路撒冷受困呢？
verses.en: “This is what King Sennacherib of Assyria says: ‘Why are you so confident that you remain in Jerusalem while it is under siege?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “On what are you trusting that [you] are living during the siege in Jerusalem.”

verses.zh: 希西家对你们说「耶和华―我们的　神必救我们脱离亚述王的手」，这不是诱惑你们，使你们受饥渴而死吗？
verses.en: Hezekiah says, “The Lord our God will rescue us from the power[NOTE:1] of the king of Assyria.” But he is misleading you, and you will die of hunger and thirst![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “hand.”
Heb “Is not Hezekiah misleading you to give you over to die by hunger and thirst, saying, ‘The Lord our God will rescue us from the hand of the king of Assyria’?’
verses.commentary:
32:11,15 "the hand of the king of Assyria" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

verses.zh: 这希西家岂不是废去耶和华的邱坛和祭坛，吩咐犹大与耶路撒冷的人说「你们当在一个坛前敬拜，在其上烧香」吗？
verses.en: Hezekiah is the one who eliminated[NOTE:1] the Lord’s[NOTE:2] high places and altars and then told Judah and Jerusalem, “At one altar you must worship and offer sacrifices.”
notes: Heb “Did not he, Hezekiah, eliminate…?” This rhetorical question presupposes a positive reply (“yes, he did”) and so has been translated here as a positive statement.
Heb “his”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我与我列祖向列邦所行的，你们岂不知道吗？列邦的神何尝能救自己的国脱离我手呢？
verses.en: Are you not aware of what I and my predecessors[NOTE:1] have done to all the nations of the surrounding lands? Have the gods of the surrounding lands actually been able to rescue their lands from my power?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 14, 15), but in this context the term does not necessarily refer to Sennacherib’s ancestors, but to his predecessors on the Assyrian throne.
Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 我列祖所灭的国，那些神中谁能救自己的民脱离我手呢？难道你们的神能救你们脱离我手吗？
verses.en: Who among all the gods of these nations whom my predecessors annihilated was able to rescue his people from my power that your God would be able to rescue you from my power?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 所以你们不要叫希西家这样欺哄诱惑你们，也不要信他；因为没有一国一邦的神能救自己的民脱离我手和我列祖的手，何况你们的神更不能救你们脱离我的手。』」
verses.en: Now don’t let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this. Don’t believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue his people from my power or the power of my predecessors. So how[NOTE:1] can your gods rescue[NOTE:2] you from my power?’”
notes: Heb “how much less.”
The verb is plural, suggesting that the preceding אֱלֹהֵיכֶם (ʾelohekhem) be translated “your gods,” rather than “your God.”

verses.zh: 西拿基立的臣仆还有别的话毁谤耶和华　神和他仆人希西家。
verses.en: Sennacherib’s[NOTE:1] servants further insulted[NOTE:2] the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah.
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Sennacherib) has been specified in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
Heb “spoke against.”
verses.commentary:
32:16-19 The king of Assyria sent letters to instill fear against Hezekiah's leadership.

- These letters insulted YHWH, v. 17.

- They asserted that no other national god had delivered their people and neither could YHWH, v. 17.

- The Assyrian messengers read this letter publicly and loudly, in Hebrew (cf. 2 Kgs. 18:26), before the walls of Jerusalem, v. 18.

- They asserted that YHWH was a manmade idol like the other gods of the nations, v. 19.

The theological stage is set! YHWH must defend His name. He is not one of the gods of the nations; He is
more powerful than the gods of Assyria.

32:16 This added comment seems to assume that the people of this post-exilic period knew the full account of
the speech of 2 Kings 18 or Isa. 36:4-10.

verses.zh: 西拿基立也写信毁谤耶和华―以色列的　神说：「列邦的神既不能救他的民脱离我手，希西家的神也不能救他的民脱离我手了。」
verses.en: He wrote letters mocking the Lord God of Israel and insulting him with these words:[NOTE:1] “The gods of the surrounding nations could not rescue their people from my power. Neither can Hezekiah’s god rescue his people from my power.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and speaking against him, saying.”
Heb “Like the gods of the nations of the lands who did not rescue their people from my hand, so the god of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my hand.”

verses.zh: 亚述王的臣仆用犹大言语向耶路撒冷城上的民大声呼叫，要惊吓他们，扰乱他们，以便取城。
verses.en: They called out loudly in the Judahite dialect to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, trying to scare and terrify them so they could seize the city.
verses.commentary: 32:18 This verse also assumes a familiarity with 2 Kgs. 18:26-37 or Isa. 36:11-20.

verses.zh: 他们论耶路撒冷的　神，如同论世上人手所造的神一样。
verses.en: They talked about the God of Jerusalem as if he were one of the man-made gods of the nations of the earth.

verses.zh: 希西家王和亚摩斯的儿子先知以赛亚因此祷告，向天呼求。
verses.en: King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this and cried out to heaven.
verses.commentary:
32:20 As is true of so much of Chronicles, its account is based on prophetic writings. Here, the great prophet Isaiah
is named (cf. Isa. 36:1-37:38).

Notice both the king and the great prophet prayed (cf. 2 Kings 19). YHWH answered in power (2 Chr. 32:21).
This powerful act of deliverance is detailed in 2 Kgs. 19:35-37.

Notice, too, the answered prayers.

- Hezekiah and Isaiah pray for military victory, v. 20.

- Hezekiah prays for healing, v. 24.

- Hezekiah prays for forgiveness, v. 26 (cf. 2 Chr. 7:14; 30:18,20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

verses.zh: 耶和华就差遣一个使者进入亚述王营中，把所有大能的勇士和官长、将帅尽都灭了。亚述王满面含羞地回到本国，进了他神的庙中，有他亲生的儿子在那里用刀杀了他。
verses.en: The Lord sent a messenger[NOTE:1] and he wiped out all the soldiers, princes, and officers in the army of the king of Assyria. So Sennacherib[NOTE:2] returned home humiliated.[NOTE:3] When he entered the temple of his god, some of his own sons[NOTE:4] struck him down with the sword.
notes: Or “an angel.”
Heb “he”; the referent (Sennacherib) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he returned with shame of face to his land.”
Heb “and some from those who went out from him, from his inward parts.”
verses.commentary:
32:21 "the Lord sent an angel" This destroying angel is probably the same one that
brought the last plague on Egypt (cf. Exodus 11).

The mentioning of angels (BDB 521) is rare in Chronicles.

- the destroying angel of 1 Chronicles 21

- the destroying angel here

This is not the "angel of the Lord" that personifies Deity but the angel that brings
judgment.

Just one lexical note. The Hebrew root translated "destroy" (BDB 470, KB 469) normally means "hide." Only
in the Hiphil stem does it rarely mean "destroy" (i.e., Exod. 23:23; 1 Kgs. 13:34; Ps. 83:4; Zech. 11:9). This implies that
there were once two different roots with the same consonants. Remember, context, not lexicons, determines word meaning.
Context, context, context!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE Lord

"his own children killed him" Sennacherib invaded in 701 b.c. (cf. 2 Kgs. 18:13, "in the fourteenth year of King
Hezekiah"). He was not assassinated until 681 b.c., some twenty years later when Esarhaddon became king.

Josephus, Antiq. 10.1.5., gives the names of the son of Adrammelch and Seraser at the temple
called Araske. The people exiled these sons to Armenia, and Esarhaddon became king (681 b.c.).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

verses.zh: 这样，耶和华救希西家和耶路撒冷的居民脱离亚述王西拿基立的手，也脱离一切仇敌的手，又赐他们四境平安。
verses.en: The Lord delivered Hezekiah and the residents of Jerusalem from the power of King Sennacherib of Assyria and from all the other nations.[NOTE:1] He made them secure on every side.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and from the hand of all.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “and he led him from all around.” However, the present translation prefers the Septuagint and Vulgate reading, which suggests an original text of וַיָּנַח לָהֶם מִסָּבִיב (vayyanakh lahem missaviv, “and he gave rest to them from all around”). See 2 Chr 15:15 and 20:30.
verses.commentary:
32:22 YHWH gave Judah "rest," which is the Chronicler's way of asserting that Hezekiah and the people's faith brought
covenant blessings (i.e., Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

NASB, NKJV, MT
"and guided them on every side"

NRSV, LXX, Vulgate
"he gave them rest on every side"

TEV
"He let the people live in peace"

NJB
"he gave them peace on every side"

JPSOA
"He provided for them on all sides"

REB
"He gave them respite on every side"

The MT has "guided" (BDB 624, KB 675, Piel IMPERFECT with waw).
The UBS Text Project, p. 480, suggests ("C" rating, meaning considerable doubt) an emendation that divides the Hebrew
letters and adds one consonant.

- MT, "and he led them" ‒ וינהלם (BDB 624, KB 675)

- LXX translates as "and he gave them rest" ‒
וינה להם

"Rest" (BDB 628, KB 679) is a recurrent covenant promise (i.e., Exod. 33:14; Deut. 3:20; 12:10; 25:19;
Josh. 1:13,15; 21:44; 22:4; 23:1; 2 Sam. 7:1,11; 1 Kgs. 5:4; 1 Chr. 22:9,18; 23:25; 2 Chr. 14:6,7; 15:15; 20:30).

verses.zh: 有许多人到耶路撒冷，将供物献与耶和华，又将宝物送给犹大王希西家。此后，希西家在列邦人的眼中看为尊大。
verses.en: Many were bringing presents[NOTE:1] to the Lord in Jerusalem and precious gifts to King Hezekiah of Judah. From that time on he was respected by[NOTE:2] all the nations.
notes: Or perhaps, “offerings.”
Heb “lifted up in the eyes of.”
verses.commentary:
32:23 YHWH's actions on behalf of His people caused both fear and honor (i.e., bringing gifts).

- fear

- Exod. 15:14-16; 23:27

- Deut. 2:25; 11:25

- Josh. 2:9

- 1 Chr. 14:17

- 2 Chr. 17:10-11; 20:29

- honor (i.e., bringing gifts)

- Exod. 3:22; 11:2; 12:35-36

- 2 Chr. 9:23-24; 17:10-11; 26:8; 32:23

verses.zh: 那时希西家病得要死，就祷告耶和华，耶和华应允他，赐他一个兆头。
verses.en: In those days Hezekiah was stricken with a terminal illness.[NOTE:1] He prayed to the Lord, who answered him and gave him a sign confirming that he would be healed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “was sick to the point of dying.”
Heb “and he spoke to him and a sign he gave to him.”
verses.commentary:
32:24 This account of Hezekiah's illness and YHWH answering his prayer is found in 2 Kgs. 10:1-11; Isa. 28:1-8.

"mortally ill" This illness is not specified in Chronicles but

- in 2 Kgs. 20:7; Isa. 38:21, it is related to a boil (BDB 1006), which was

- one of the plagues on Egypt ‒ Exod. 9:9-11

- one of the consequences of covenant disobedience ‒ Deut. 28:27,35

- Josephus, Antiq. 10.2.1., calls it "distemper" (physical) and "melancholy circumstances" (mental, i.e., no heir)

"gave him a sign" The miracle is recorded in 2 Kgs. 20:8-9. The shadow from the sun moved backwards on the steps.

verses.zh: 希西家却没有照他所蒙的恩报答耶和华；因他心里骄傲，所以忿怒要临到他和犹大并耶路撒冷。
verses.en: But Hezekiah was ungrateful; he had a proud attitude, provoking God to be angry at him, as well as Judah and Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.tn Heb “but not according to the benefit [given] to him did Hezekiah repay, for his heart was high, and there was anger against him and against Judah and Jerusalem.”
verses.commentary:
32:25 The account of Hezekiah's prideful act and its consequences is found in 2 Kgs. 20:12-21 (note v. 31 here).

This does show that even godly people in good times still have a pull towards self! This is the residue of the
Fall of Genesis 3. Hezekiah's pride brought terrible consequences, to his descendants and to all the people of Judah. His sin
affected the whole nation! This same theological issue of corporality can be seen in

- Adam's sin of Genesis 3 ‒ Rom. 5:12-21

- Achan's sin at Jericho ‒ Joshua 7

- David's sin with Bathsheba ‒ 2 Samuel 11

- Solomon's sin in his old age with his foreign wives ‒ 1 Kgs. 11:1-8

- Messiah's substitutionary death ‒ Isaiah 53

"heart" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEART.

verses.zh: 但希西家和耶路撒冷的居民觉得心里骄傲，就一同自卑，以致耶和华的忿怒在希西家的日子没有临到他们。
verses.en: But then Hezekiah and the residents of Jerusalem humbled themselves and abandoned their pride, and the Lord was not angry with them for the rest of Hezekiah’s reign.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Hezekiah humbled himself in the height of his heart, he and the residents of Jerusalem, and the anger of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.”
verses.commentary:
32:26 "humbled himself" This VERB (BDB 488, KB 484, Niphal
IMPERFECT with waw, cf. 2 Chr. 7:14; 12:6,7,12; 30:11; 33:12,19,23; 34:27) is an idiom for repentance.
Repentance changes hearts, minds, and circumstances.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

verses.zh: 希西家大有尊荣资财，建造府库，收藏金银、宝石、香料、盾牌，和各样的宝器，
verses.en: Hezekiah was very wealthy and greatly respected. He made storehouses for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all his other valuable possessions.
verses.commentary:
32:27 "spices" It seems unusual to modern westerners that perfumes (BDB 141, lit. "spices") were a source of
wealth (cf. 1 Kgs. 10:2,10,25; 2 Chr. 9:1,24; Ezek. 27:22). In 2 Kgs. 20:13 and Isa. 39:2 "spices" are linked with "precious
oils" (BDB 1032 and BDB 373 II). See NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 774-775.

The MT has "shields" (BDB 171) after "spices" and before "all kinds of courtly vessels" (BDB 479
CONSTRUCT BDB 326). The NET Bible suggests an emendation unsupported by the ancient versions
which changes "shields," מגנים to "precious items,"

מגדנום (BDB 550, cf. v. 23).

verses.zh: 又建造仓房，收藏五谷、新酒，和油，又为各类牲畜盖棚立圈；
verses.en: He made storerooms for the harvest of grain, wine, and olive oil, and stalls for all his various kinds of livestock and his flocks.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and stalls for all beasts and beasts, and flocks for the stalls.” The repetition of בְּהֵמָה (behemah, “beast”) here indicates various kinds of livestock.

verses.zh: 并且建立城邑，还有许多的羊群牛群，因为　神赐他极多的财产。
verses.en: He built royal cities[NOTE:1] and owned a large number of sheep and cattle, for God gave him a huge amount of possessions.
notes: Heb “and cities he made for himself.”
verses.commentary:
32:29

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, LXX
"cities"

NJB
"donkeys"

REB, Pehsitta
omits "cities"

The UBS Text Project, p. 481, gives "cities" an "A" rating. The NEB and REB follow the Peshitta, which
lists only animals. The NOUN "cities" (BDB 746) has the same consonants as "donkeys" (BDB 747). Donkey
fits better the list of animals in this verse. Donkeys were the royal mount of Israel's kings.

Large flocks were a symbol of agricultural blessing from YHWH (i.e., Lev. 26:2-6) for covenant obedience
(i.e., Deut. 8:13; 15:14; 28:4).

verses.zh: 这希西家也塞住基训的上源，引水直下，流在大卫城的西边。希西家所行的事尽都亨通。
verses.en: Hezekiah dammed up the source of the waters of the Upper Gihon and directed them down to the west side of the City of David.[NOTE:1] Hezekiah succeeded in all that he did.
notes: The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
verses.commentary:
32:30 The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1816, suggests this verse may refer to the Siloam tunnel (cf. 2 Kgs. 20:20). See
R. K. Harrison, Introduction to the Old Testament, p. 128.

verses.zh: 惟有一件事，就是巴比伦王差遣使者来见希西家，访问国中所现的奇事；这件事　神离开他，要试验他，好知道他心内如何。
verses.en: So when the envoys arrived from the Babylonian officials to visit him and inquire about the sign that occurred in the land,[NOTE:1] God left him alone to test him in order to know his true motives.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and when the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who sent to him to inquire concerning the sign which was in the land, [arrived].”
Heb “to know all [that was] in his heart.”
verses.commentary:
32:31 "the wonder that had happened in the land" What "wonder" (lit. "sign," BDB 68, cf. 2 Chr. 32:24)?

- Because the term "wonder/sign" is used in vv. 24 and 31, most think it was Hezekiah's healing (cf. 2 Kgs. 20:12); possibly
because they were astral worshipers and the "sign" involved the sun.

- But "in the land," along with "envoys of the rulers of Babylon, who were enemies of Assyria," I think it was the miraculous
defeat of Sennacherib's large army (v. 1) who had not been defeated before this (vv. 21-22; cf. 2 Kgs. 19:35-37). Also note
the information in 2 Kgs. 20:13-21 and Edwin M. Yamauchi, The Stones and the Scriptures, p. 80.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TESTS HIS PEOPLE

"that He might know all that was in his heart" This is an idiom, not a theological affirmation, of "Open Theism."
God often "tests" his people to demonstrate their faith (i.e., Genesis 3; 22; see Special Topic above).

We must remember that God knows the motives of the human heart, which determine the appropriateness or
inappropriateness of every action (cf. 1 Sam. 2:7; 16:7; 1 Kgs. 8:39; 1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 6:30;Ps. 7:9; 44:21; 139:1-4;
Pro. 15:11; 21:2; Jer. 11:20; 17:9-10; 20:12; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27).

verses.zh: 希西家其余的事和他的善行都写在亚摩斯的儿子先知以赛亚的默示书上和犹大、以色列的诸王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Hezekiah’s reign, including his faithful deeds, are recorded in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, included in the Scroll of the Kings of Judah and Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the rest of the deeds of Hezekiah and his faithful acts, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet upon the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.”
verses.commentary:
32:32-33 This is a typical summary statement of a king's reign. Notice the two sources of information used by the Chronicler.

- writing of Isaiah

- royal document of the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel

- other sources about this period are found in James B. Pritchard, The Ancient Near East, vol. 1.

- Sennacherib's siege of Jerusalem, pp. 199-201

- Lachish Ostraca, pp. 212-214

- also note Esarhaddon's Syro-Palestinian campaign, 2 Chronicles 33, pp. 201-202

The Chronicler uniquely used prophetic sources (cf. 1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. 9:29; 12:15; 13:22; 24:19-21; 26:22;
32:32; 33:19.

32:32 "his deeds of devotion" This is a secular use of the covenant word hesed (cf. Neh. 13:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

verses.zh: 希西家与他列祖同睡，葬在大卫子孙的高陵上。他死的时候，犹大人和耶路撒冷的居民都尊敬他。他儿子玛拿西接续他作王。
verses.en: Hezekiah passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried on the ascent of the tombs of the descendants of David. All the people of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem buried him with great honor.[NOTE:2] His son Manasseh replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”
Heb “and honor they did to him in his death, all Judah and the residents of Jerusalem.”
verses.commentary:
32:33 "slept with his fathers" This is a Hebrew idiom for being buried in the royal tombs. The OT asserted a
conscious, but gloomy, afterlife until judgment day (i.e., Dan. 12:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

"honored him" Honor (BDB 468 II) is used of several godly kings.

- David ‒ 1 Chr. 29:12,28

- Solomon ‒ 1 Kgs. 3:13; 2 Chr. 1:11-12

- Jehoshaphat ‒ 2 Chr. 17:5; 18:1

- Hezekiah ‒ here

Mostly the term is used of YHWH giving them honor, but here of the people of Judah and Jerusalem honoring
Hezekiah at his burial.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What "acts of faithfulness" is 2 Chr. 32:1 referring to?

- Why did the Chronicler not mention Hezekiah trying to buy off Sennacherib?

- Why does Isaiah 22 make Hezekiah's preparations for the coming Assyrian siege evil, while the Chronicler affirms them?

- Why are 2 Chr. 32:7-8 such wonderful theological verses?

- How is 2 Chr. 32:10 the theological key to the whole chapter?

- List the reasons given by Sennacherib's envoy why Judah should not resist.

- How did YHWH spare Jerusalem?

- How does this chapter show Hezekiah's great faith and yet human failure?
